narr: The Calf Canyon burn scar had received a well deserved break from flash flooding impacts for a couple of weeks at the end of August and into early September. However, monsoon season was not officially over yet, and a return of moisture resulted in numerous thunderstorms developing across the area on September 10, 2022. Unfortunately, the Calf Canyon burn scar was impacted as a nearly stationary thunderstorms dropped over two inches of rain on the southern portion of the large burn scar which caused flash flooding in the area.
ev: A nearly stationary thunderstorm over El Porvenir produced over two inches of rainfall on this area of the Calf Canyon burn scar. This caused flash flooding on Beaver Creek and Gallinas Creek with significant debris found on Highway 65. The IMET on duty found several locations along Highway 65 that were covered in tree debris, rocks, and mud. Some buildings along the roadway were inundated with a couple of feet of water. The IMET also noted that water had threatened homes in the area as well, but these homes seemed to have been protected with sandbagging. Damages are estimated.
